text:
maya: Heads up — CI pipeline for sample-app failed on the publish job after the latest typegen + package bump. Looks like semver/changelog mismatch plus an auth retry test is failing.

ci-bot: build #4589 | publish: FAILED (exit 1) 
ci-bot: see logs: https://ci.redwood/4589/logs/publish

maya: paste of the failing snippet from the logs:
```
Error: changelog check failed: package.json version 2.0.0 -> changelog contains only patch/minor entries
  at checkChangelog (/workspace/scripts/release-check.js:43:15)
Typegen: generated types differ from committed files (diff in packages/sdk/src/types.ts)
Test: auth/retry.spec.ts › retry logic › should retry 3 times on 500
  Expected: 3
  Received: 2
```

alex: ugh. Any idea which step bumped package.json to 2.0.0? I only touched onboarding sample wording.

maya: I ran `yarn typegen` locally after pulling main and it updated a bunch of field optionality in the generated types — maybe that triggered a version bump in the sample-app package? Not sure why semver-major though.

jonathan: quick guess: the release script auto-bumps if typegen diffs are present and "breaking"? The breaking detection is heuristic; last change to our type mapping made some fields optional -> major.

sam: Also, the auth test failure might be from the generated client changing the retry defaults (we recently added per-client retry policy). If typegen changed the default from 3 -> 2, that would explain the test.

maya: Good call. Reproduced locally: after running `yarn typegen` in packages/sample-app, `packages/sdk/package.json` shows "version": "2.0.0" and `packages/sdk/src/retry.ts` default maxRetries = 2.

alex: So we have 2 separate cascaded issues: (1) typegen change that altered defaults (should be flagged in change log PR), and (2) release automation that bumped semver to major automatically. Both should not have landed without a human ack.

jonathan: Proposed immediate remediation: revert the publish job (roll back the release tag), open a tiny PR with the regenerated types but restore retry default to 3, and update changelog entry describing the non-breaking changes. Then run typegen + changelog lint locally before re-trying the publish.

maya: I'll open the rollback PR and the follow-up. Assigning myself.

sam: For CI: can we add a cheap gate that fails any automatic semver bump to major unless a "BREAKING:" token exists in PR body or changelog? Not sure current bot checks that.

alex: I like the gate; minimal change: release-bot should require explicit "major" label to auto-bump to major. Otherwise default to patch.

jonathan: I'll draft a tiny change to release-bot this afternoon. Also adding a test in auth/retry.spec that asserts SDK default stays stable unless changelog has BREAKING note. Keeps us honest.

ci-bot: action required: rollback candidate created: refs/tags/release-2.0.0 -> rollback pending (maya)

maya: Created PR #7891: "rollback/release-2.0.0 - revert auto-major bump; fix retry default" with the following steps in the description:
- Revert publish tag
- Regenerate types with patch-level mapping (keep semantics)
- Manually set retry default back to 3
- Add changelog entry under Unreleased explaining the change and why it's not breaking

maya: link: https://git.redwood/pr/7891 

sam: Thanks. After PR merges, can we add a CI job that runs `node scripts/release-check.js` in draft mode on PRs touching typegen outputs? Would have flagged this.

alex: filing follow-up issue to add draft-mode changelog check and stricter release-bot locking. I'll assign to release infra.

jonathan: TL;DR: rollback then re-release after manual review. Add guardrails: require explicit BREAKING flag for auto-major and add unit test for retry default.

maya: ok I'm on it. Will ping here when publish retries. :thumbsup:
